# Data Source: stripe_issuing_dispute

A dispute of an Issuing transaction, on a connected account, with the evidence for it. Look one up by its `id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "connected_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "The connected account the object lives on."
}

provider "stripe" {
  alias          = "connected"
  stripe_account = var.connected_account
}

data "stripe_issuing_dispute" "unrecognised" {
  provider = stripe.connected
  id       = "idp_1MvSieLkdIwHu7ixOeFkD4Dx"
}

output "dispute_status" {
  value = data.stripe_issuing_dispute.unrecognised.status
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the issuing dispute to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `amount` - The dispute amount in the card's currency and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). If not set, defaults to the full transaction amount.
* `balance_transactions` - List of balance transactions associated with the dispute. See [`balance_transactions`](#balance_transactions) below.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - The currency the `transaction` was made in.
* `evidence` - Evidence provided for the dispute. See [`evidence`](#evidence) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `loss_reason` - The enum that describes the dispute loss outcome. If the dispute is not lost, this field will be absent. New enum values may be added in the future, so be sure to handle unknown values. Possible values: `cardholder_authentication_issuer_liability`, `eci5_token_transaction_with_tavv`, `excess_disputes_in_timeframe`, `has_not_met_the_minimum_dispute_amount_requirements`, `invalid_duplicate_dispute`, `invalid_incorrect_amount_dispute`, `invalid_no_authorization`, `invalid_use_of_disputes`, `merchandise_delivered_or_shipped`, `merchandise_or_service_as_described`, `not_cancelled`, `other`, `refund_issued`, `submitted_beyond_allowable_time_limit`, `transaction_3ds_required`, `transaction_approved_after_prior_fraud_dispute`, `transaction_authorized`, `transaction_electronically_read`, `transaction_qualifies_for_visa_easy_payment_service`, `transaction_unattended`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `status` - Current status of the dispute. Possible values: `expired`, `lost`, `submitted`, `unsubmitted`, `won`.
* `transaction` - The ID of the issuing transaction to create a dispute for. For transaction on Treasury FinancialAccounts, use `treasury.received_debit`.
* `treasury` - [Treasury](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury) details related to this dispute if it was created on a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury/financial_accounts) See [`treasury`](#treasury) below.

<a id="balance_transactions"></a>
### `balance_transactions`

The `balance_transactions` attribute is a list. Each element holds a balance transaction, with the attributes of the [`stripe_balance_transaction`](../data-sources/balance_transaction) data source and `object`, the name of its type.

<a id="evidence"></a>
### `evidence`

The `evidence` attribute supports:

* `canceled` - See [`evidence.canceled`](#evidence.canceled) below.
* `duplicate` - See [`evidence.duplicate`](#evidence.duplicate) below.
* `fraudulent` - See [`evidence.fraudulent`](#evidence.fraudulent) below.
* `merchandise_not_as_described` - See [`evidence.merchandise_not_as_described`](#evidence.merchandise_not_as_described) below.
* `no_valid_authorization` - See [`evidence.no_valid_authorization`](#evidence.no_valid_authorization) below.
* `not_received` - See [`evidence.not_received`](#evidence.not_received) below.
* `other` - See [`evidence.other`](#evidence.other) below.
* `reason` - The reason for filing the dispute. Its value will match the field containing the evidence. Possible values: `canceled`, `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `merchandise_not_as_described`, `no_valid_authorization`, `not_received`, `other`, `service_not_as_described`.
* `service_not_as_described` - See [`evidence.service_not_as_described`](#evidence.service_not_as_described) below.

<a id="evidence.canceled"></a>
### `evidence.canceled`

The `evidence.canceled` attribute supports:

* `additional_documentation` - (ID of a [file upload](https://stripe.com/docs/guides/file-upload)) Additional documentation supporting the dispute.
* `canceled_at` - Date when order was canceled.
* `cancellation_policy_provided` - Whether the cardholder was provided with a cancellation policy.
* `cancellation_reason` - Reason for canceling the order.
* `expected_at` - Date when the cardholder expected to receive the product.
* `explanation` - Explanation of why the cardholder is disputing this transaction.
* `product_description` - Description of the merchandise or service that was purchased.
* `product_type` - Whether the product was a merchandise or service. Possible values: `merchandise`, `service`.
* `return_status` - Result of cardholder's attempt to return the product. Possible values: `merchant_rejected`, `successful`.
* `returned_at` - Date when the product was returned or attempted to be returned.

<a id="evidence.duplicate"></a>
### `evidence.duplicate`

The `evidence.duplicate` attribute supports:

* `additional_documentation` - (ID of a [file upload](https://stripe.com/docs/guides/file-upload)) Additional documentation supporting the dispute.
* `card_statement` - (ID of a [file upload](https://stripe.com/docs/guides/file-upload)) Copy of the card statement showing that the product had already been paid for.
* `cash_receipt` - (ID of a [file upload](https://stripe.com/docs/guides/file-upload)) Copy of the receipt showing that the product had been paid for in cash.
* `check_image` - (ID of a [file upload](https://stripe.com/docs/guides/file-upload)) Image of the front and back of the check that was used to pay for the product.
* `explanation` - Explanation of why the cardholder is disputing this transaction.
* `original_transaction` - Transaction (e.g., ipi_...) that the disputed transaction is a duplicate of. Of the two or more transactions that are copies of each other, this is original undisputed one.

<a id="treasury"></a>
### `treasury`

The `treasury` attribute supports:

* `debit_reversal` - The Treasury [DebitReversal](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury/debit_reversals) representing this Issuing dispute
* `received_debit` - The Treasury [ReceivedDebit](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury/received_debits) that is being disputed.
